Text: Wow, there are so many Blacktip Reef Sharks! As the top hunter they need lots to eat. Try adding more prey like Fringelip Mullet or Yellowstripe Scad, or remove a shark or two to balance the reef!
The Blacktip Reef Sharks are the top hunters here, so nothing preys on them. If they look unhappy, it is usually because they are low on food!
Oh no, the Blacktip Reef Sharks are going hungry! They have nothing to hunt. Try adding some Fringelip Mullet or Yellowstripe Scad for them to eat!
Whoa, the Bluefin Trevally are taking over! They are a top hunter, so try adding more prey like Yellowstripe Scad for them, or remove a few to balance things out!
The Bluefin Trevally are fast top hunters, so nothing chases them. Keep an eye on their food instead!
The Bluefin Trevally are starving! Try adding some Yellowstripe Scad or Fringelip Mullet so they have something to hunt!
There sure are a lot of Brown Marbled Groupers! They are big hunters, so try adding more prey like Bullethead Parrotfish, or remove a grouper or two to keep balance!
The Brown Marbled Groupers are strong hunters with no predators of their own. If they struggle, check their food supply!
Uh oh, the Brown Marbled Groupers have run out of food! Try adding some Bullethead Parrotfish or Fringelip Mullet for them to eat!
So many Giant Morays! These sneaky hunters have no predators, so try adding more prey like Streaked Spinefoot, or remove a moray to balance the reef!
The Giant Morays are ambush hunters that nothing preys on. If they are unhappy, they are probably hungry!
The Giant Morays are hungry with nothing to hunt! Try adding some Yellowstripe Scad or Streaked Spinefoot to feed them!
Wow, the Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays are everywhere and nothing is hunting them! Try adding a Blacktip Reef Shark to keep their numbers in check!
Oh no, the Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays are getting eaten up fast! Try removing a Blacktip Reef Shark to give them a chance to recover!
The Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays find their food buried in the sand, so they never go hungry here!
Uh oh, the Bullethead Parrotfish are taking over the reef! Try adding a hunter like a Brown Marbled Grouper or a Bluefin Trevally to balance things out!

The Bullethead Parrotfish love scraping algae off the coral, so they always have plenty to eat!
So many Eyestripe Surgeonfish! With no predators around they just keep growing. Try adding a Giant Moray or a Russell's Snapper to hunt a few!
The Eyestripe Surgeonfish are disappearing fast, too many hunters are after them! Try removing a Giant Moray or a Russell's Snapper to give them a break!
The Eyestripe Surgeonfish graze on algae all day, so they always have plenty to munch on!
